source_text:
Ἆρον ἀπὸ σεαυτοῦ, φησί, τὴν λύπην: καὶ γὰρ αὕτη ἀδελφή ἐστι τῆς διψυχίας καὶ τῆς ὀξυχολίας.
Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, ἀδελφή ἐστι τούτων; ἄλλο γάρ μοι δοκεῖ εἶναι ὀξυχολία καὶ ἄλλο διψυχία καὶ ἄλλο λύπη. Ἀσύνετος εἶ ἄνθρωπε, φησί, καὶ οὐ νοεῖς, ὅτι ἡ λύπη πάντων τῶν πνευμάτων πονηροτέρα ἐστὶ καὶ δεινοτάτη τοῖς δούλοις τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ παρὰ πάντα τὰ πνεύματα καταφθείρει τὸν ἄνθρωπον καὶ ἐκτρίβει τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον καὶ πάλιν σώζει;
Ἐγώ, φημί, κύριε, ἀσύνετός εἰμι καὶ οὐ συνίω τὰς παραβολὰς ταύτας. πῶς γὰρ δύναται ἐκτρίβειν καὶ πάλιν σώζειν, οὐ νοῶ.
Ἄκουε, φησίν: οἱ μηδέποτε ἐρευνήσαντες περὶ τῆς ἀληθείας μηδὲ ἐπιζητήσαντες περὶ τῆς θεότητος, πιστεύσαντες δὲ μόνον, ἐμπεφυρμένοι δὲ πραγματείαις καὶ πλούτῳ καὶ φιλίαις ἐθνικαῖς καὶ ἄλλαις πολλαῖς πραγματείαις τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου: ὅσοι οὖν τούτοις πρόσκεινται, οὐ νοοῦσι τὰς παραβολὰς τῆς θεότητος: ἐπισκοτοῦνται γὰρ ὑπὸ τούτων τῶν πράξεων καὶ καταφθείρονται καὶ γίνονται κεχερσωμένοι.
καθὼς οἱ ἀμπελῶνες οἱ καλοί, ὅταν ἀμελείας τύχωσι, χερσοῦνται ἀπὸ τῶν ἀκανθῶν καὶ βοτανῶν ποικίλων, οὕτως οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ πιστεύσαντες καὶ εἰς ταύτας τὰς πράξεις τὰς πολλὰς ἐμπίπτοντες τὰς προειρημένας, ἀποπλανῶνται ἀπὸ τῆς διανοίας αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐδὲν ὅλως νοοῦσι περὶ δικαιοσύνης, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὅταν ἀκούσωσι περὶ θεότητος καὶ ἀληθείας, ὁ νοῦς αὐτῶν περὶ τὴν πρᾶξιν αὐτῶν καταγίνεται, καὶ οὐδὲν ὅλως νοοῦσιν.
οἱ δὲ φόβον ἔχοντες θεοῦ καὶ ἐρευνῶντες περὶ θεότητος καὶ ἀληθείας καὶ τὴν καρδίαν ἔχοντες πρὸς τὸν κύριον, πάντα τὰ λεγόμενα αὐτοῖς τάχιον νοοῦσι καὶ συνίουσιν, ὅτι ἔχουσι τὸν φόβον τοῦ κυρίου ἐν ἑαυτοῖς: ὅπου γὰρ ὁ κύριος κατοικεῖ, ἐκεῖ καὶ σύνεσις πολλή. κολλήθητι οὖν τῷ κυρίῳ, καὶ πάντα συνήσεις καὶ νοήσεις.
Ἄκουε οὖν, φησίν, ἀνόητε, πῶς ἡ λύπη ἐκτρίβει τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον καὶ πάλιν σώζει:
ὅταν ὁ δίψυχος ἐπιβάληται πρᾶξίν τινα καὶ ταύτης ἀποτύχῃ διὰ τὴν διψυχίαν αὐτοῦ, ἡ λύπη αὕτη εἰσπορεύεται εἰς τὸν ἄνθρωπον καὶ λυπεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον καὶ ἐκτρίβει αὐτό.
εἶτα πάλιν ἡ ὀξυχολία ὅταν κολληθῇ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ περὶ πράγματός τινος, καὶ λίαν πικρανθῇ, πάλιν ἡ λύπη εἰσπορεύεται εἰς τὴν καρδίαν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τοῦ ὀξυχολήσαντος, καὶ λυπεῖται ἐπὶ τῇ πράξει αὐτοῦ ᾗ ἔπραξε καὶ μετανοεῖ, ὅτι πονηρὸν εἰργάσατο.
αὕτη οὖν ἡ λύπη δοκεῖ σωτηρίαν ἔχειν, ὅτι τὸ πονηρὸν πράξας μετενόησεν. ἀμφότεραι οὖν αἱ πράξεις λυποῦσι τὸ πνεῦμα: ἡ μὲν διψυχία, ὅτι οὐκ ἐπέτυχε τῆς πράξεως αὐτῆς, ἡ δὲ ὀξυχολία λυπεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα, ὅτι ἔπραξε τὸ πονηρόν. ἀμφότερα οὖν λυπηρά ἐστι τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ, ἡ διψυχία καὶ ἡ ὀξυχολία.
ἆρον οὖν ἀπὸ σεαυτοῦ τὴν λύπην καὶ μὴ θλῖβε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τὸ ἐν σοὶ κατοικοῦν, μήποτε ἐντεύξηται τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἀποστῇ ἀπὸ σοῦ.
τὸ γὰρ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ τὸ δοθὲν εἰς τὴν σάρκα ταύτην λύπην οὐχ ὑποφέρει οὐδὲ στενοχωρίαν.
Ἔνδυσαι οὖν τὴν ἱλαρότητα, τὴν πάντοτε ἔχουσαν χάριν παρὰ τῷ θεῷ καὶ εὐπρόσδεκτον οὖσαν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἐντρύφα ἐν αὐτῇ. πᾶς γὰρ ἱλαρὸς ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὰ ἐργάζεται καὶ ἀγαθὰ φρονεῖ καὶ καταφρονεῖ τῆς λύπης.
ὁ δὲ λυπηρὸς ἀνὴρ πάντοτε πονηρεύεται: πρῶτον μὲν πονηρεύεται, ὅτι λυπεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τὸ δοθὲν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἱλαρόν: δεύτερον δὲ λυπῶν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἀνομίαν ἐργάζεται, μὴ ἐντυγχάνων μηδὲ ἐξομολογούμενος τῷ κυρίῳ. Πάντοτε γὰρ λυπηροῦ ἀνδρὸς ἡ ἔντευξις οὐκ ἔχει δύναμιν τοῦ ἀναβῆναι ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τοῦ θεοῦ.
Διατί, φημί, οὐκ ἀναβαίνει ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον ἡ ἔντευξις τοῦ λυπουμένου; Ὅτι, φησίν, ἡ λύπη ἐγκάθηται εἰς τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ. μεμιγμένη οὖν ἡ λύπη μετὰ τῆς ἐντεύξεως οὐκ ἀφίησι τὴν ἔντευξιν ἀναβῆναι καθαρὰν ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον. ὥσπερ γὰρ ὄξος καὶ οἶνος μεμιγμένα ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ τὴν αὐτὴν ἡδονὴν οὐκ ἔχουσιν, οὕτω καὶ ἡ λύπη μεμιγμένη μετὰ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος τὴν αὐτὴν ἔντευξιν οὐκ ἔχει.
καθάρισον οὖν σεαυτὸν ἀπὸ τῆς λύπης τῆς πονηρᾶς ταύτης, καὶ ζήσῃ τῷ θεῷ: καὶ πάντες ζήσονται τῷ θεῷ, ὅσοι ἂν ἀποβάλωσιν ἀφ̓ ἑαυτῶν τὴν λύπην καὶ ἐνδύσωνται πᾶσαν ἱλαρότητα.
thought_title: Grief, the sister of double-mindedness and anger
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the tenth commandment: put away grief and put on cheerfulness. He explains how grief can wear out the Holy Spirit, and how the grief that leads to repentance can save.
pass_a_gloss: Take away from yourself, he says, the grief: for also this [grief] sister is of the double-mindedness and of the anger. How, I say, lord, sister is [it] of these? For one thing to me seems to be anger and another double-mindedness and another grief. Foolish you are, man, he says, and you do not understand, that the grief of all the spirits more wicked is and most terrible to the servants of God and beyond all the spirits destroys the man and rubs out the spirit the holy and again saves? I, I say, lord, foolish am and I do not understand the parables these. For how can [it] rub out and again save, I do not understand. Listen, he says: the [ones] never having searched about the truth nor having sought about the divinity, but having believed only, but [being] entangled in business affairs and wealth and friendships pagan and other many affairs of this age: as many therefore as to these [things] are devoted, they do not understand the parables of the divinity: for they are darkened by these deeds and are corrupted and become barren. Just as the vineyards the good, whenever of neglect they meet, are made barren by the thorns and weeds various, so the men the [ones] having believed and into these deeds the many falling the [ones] previously mentioned, are led astray from their mind, and nothing at all they understand about righteousness, but also whenever they hear about divinity and truth, their mind about their business is occupied, and nothing at all they understand. But the [ones] fear having of God and searching about divinity and truth and the heart having toward the Lord, all the [things] said to them more quickly they understand and comprehend, because they have the fear of the Lord in themselves: for where the Lord dwells, there also understanding much [is]. Cleave therefore to the Lord, and all [things] you will comprehend and understand. Listen therefore, he says, foolish [one], how the grief rubs out the spirit the holy and again saves: whenever the double-minded [one] undertakes a deed some and in this fails through the double-mindedness of him, this grief enters into the man and grieves the spirit the holy and rubs out it. Then again the anger whenever it cleaves to the man about a matter some, and very [he] is embittered, again the grief enters into the heart of the man of the [one] having become angry, and he is grieved over the deed of him which he did and repents, because evil he worked. This therefore the grief seems salvation to have, because the evil [thing] having done he repented. Both therefore the deeds grieve the spirit: the one double-mindedness, because it did not succeed in the deed of it, and the anger grieves the spirit, because it did the evil [thing]. Both therefore grievous are to the spirit to the holy, the double-mindedness and the anger. Take away therefore from yourself the grief and do not afflict the spirit the holy the [one] in you dwelling, lest ever it intercede with God and depart from you. For the spirit of God the [one] given into this flesh grief does not bear nor distress. Put on therefore the cheerfulness, the [one] always having favor with God and acceptable being to him, and delight in it. For every cheerful man good [things] works and good [things] thinks and despises the grief. But the grieving man always does evil: first indeed he does evil, because he grieves the spirit the holy the [one] given to the man cheerful: second but grieving the spirit the holy lawlessness he works, not interceding nor confessing to the Lord. For always of a grieving man the intercession does not have power to go up to the altar of God. Why, I say, does not go up to the altar the intercession of the [one] grieving? Because, he says, the grief sits in the heart of him. Mixed therefore the grief with the intercession does not allow the intercession to go up pure to the altar. For just as vinegar and wine mixed together the same pleasure do not have, so also the grief mixed with the holy spirit the same intercession does not have. Cleanse therefore yourself from the grief the evil this, and you will live to God: and all will live to God, as many as would cast away from themselves the grief and put on all cheerfulness.

choices.why: The Shepherd treats λύπη as a distinct evil spirit, sister to double-mindedness and anger; 'grief' keeps the emotional weight and personified force without softening it into 'sadness' or 'sorrow'.
The verb means to wear away or obliterate by rubbing; 'rubs out' preserves the physical, destructive image applied to the Holy Spirit, which 'wears away' or 'erases' would weaken.
The verb χερσόω means to make land dry, waste, or uncultivated; 'made barren' fits the vineyard simile and the spiritual desolation described.
The term denotes a bright, glad disposition that is pleasing to God; 'cheerfulness' captures the active, visible quality better than 'joy' or 'gladness,' which are more abstract.
In this context it refers to the believer's petition or appeal to God, especially as it ascends to the altar; 'intercession' preserves the liturgical and prayerful sense.
The perfect participle of ἐμφύρω means mixed up in or defiled by; 'entangled' conveys being caught up in worldly affairs so as to be unable to understand divine things.

pass_b_english: “Rid yourself of grief,” the Shepherd said, “for grief too is a sister of double-mindedness and of anger.”

“Sir,” I said, “how is grief a sister of these? Anger seems to me one thing, double-mindedness another, and grief another.” “You are without understanding, man,” he said. “Do you not see that grief is more wicked than all the spirits, and most terrible for the servants of God? More than all the spirits it ruins a person and wears out the Holy Spirit, and then again it saves.”
“Sir,” I said, “I am without understanding, and I do not understand these parables. How grief can wear out and then again save, I do not grasp.”

“Listen,” he said. “There are those who have never searched for the truth or inquired about divinity. They have only believed, and they are mixed up in business and wealth and friendships among the nations and the many other affairs of this age. All who are devoted to these things fail to grasp the parables of divinity. For they are darkened by these activities, and ruined, and they become barren.

“Good vineyards, when they are neglected, are made barren by thorns and weeds of many kinds. In the same way, people who have believed and then fall into these many activities already named find their minds led astray, and they grasp nothing at all about righteousness. Even when they hear about divinity and truth, their mind is taken up with their own business, and they grasp nothing at all.

“But there are those who have the fear of God, who search into divinity and truth and have their heart set toward the Lord. They quickly grasp and understand everything that is said to them, because they have the fear of the Lord in themselves. For where the Lord dwells, there is much understanding as well. So cling to the Lord, and you will understand and grasp everything.
“Hear then, foolish man,” he said, “how grief wears out the Holy Spirit and then again saves.
“When the double-minded man takes some work in hand and fails in it because of his double-mindedness, this grief enters into the man. It grieves the Holy Spirit and wears it out.

“Then again, when anger clings to a man over some matter and he becomes very bitter, grief again enters the heart of the man who was angry. He is grieved at the deed he has done, and he repents, because he did evil.

“So this grief seems to hold salvation, because the man who did evil repented. Both actions, then, grieve the Spirit. Double-mindedness grieves the Spirit because it did not succeed in what it set out to do, and anger grieves the Spirit because it did what is evil. So both are grievous to the Holy Spirit, double-mindedness and anger.
“So rid yourself of grief, and do not press hard upon the Holy Spirit that dwells in you, or it may appeal to God and depart from you.
“For the Spirit of God that was given to this flesh does not bear grief or anguish.
“So put on cheerfulness, which always finds favor with God and is welcome to him, and take your delight in it. For every cheerful man does good things and thinks good things and despises grief.

“But the grieving man always does wickedly. First, he does wickedly because he grieves the Holy Spirit, which was given to man as a cheerful Spirit. Second, by grieving the Holy Spirit he works lawlessness, for he neither prays nor confesses to the Lord. For the prayer of a grieving man never has the power to rise to the altar of God.”

“Why,” I said, “does the prayer of the grieving man not rise to the altar?” “Because,” he said, “grief sits in his heart. So the grief is mixed with the prayer, and it does not let the prayer rise pure to the altar. For vinegar and wine, mixed together, do not have the same pleasant taste. In the same way, when grief is mixed with the Holy Spirit, the prayer is not the same.
“So cleanse yourself of this wicked grief, and you will live to God. And all will live to God who cast grief away from themselves and put on all cheerfulness.”

problems.why: ἐντυγχάνω means 'intercede/plead (to God)', not 'intercede against'; no hostile sense

edits.old: lest it intercede with God against you and depart from you.
edits.new: lest it intercede to God and depart from you.

fixed: Changed 'intercede with God against you' to 'intercede to God' to remove the hostile sense not present in the Greek.

problems.quote: lest it intercede to God and depart from you
problems.source_quote: μήποτε ἐντεύξηται τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἀποστῇ ἀπὸ σοῦ
problems.why: Source means 'lest it entreat God and depart from you'—i.e., the Spirit departs. 'Intercede' implies the Spirit advocates for Hermas, but the warning is that grief drives the Spirit away.
problems.fix: lest it entreat God and depart from you
problems.ruling: ἐντεύξηται means 'entreat/plead,' not 'intercede for'; the Spirit pleads to leave, not advocates.

problems.why: 'Never has power' adds temporal 'never' not in source; source says 'does not have power to ascend', a statement of incapacity, not 'never' has power. This changes modality by adding temporal absoluteness.
problems.fix: does not have power to ascend
problems.ruling: Source οὐκ ἔχει δύναμιν is present-tense incapacity; 'never has power' adds temporal absoluteness not in Greek.

problems.why: The Greek ἱλαρόν is neuter singular, agreeing with πνεῦμα (spirit), not 'as a cheerful spirit' but 'cheerful'—the Spirit was given cheerful/glad. 'As a cheerful spirit' makes ἱλαρόν a separate spirit rather than the quality of the Holy Spirit given.
problems.ruling: ἱλαρόν is neuter agreeing with πνεῦμα; 'as a cheerful spirit' misreads it as a separate spirit, changing meaning.

edits.old: lest it intercede to God and depart from you
edits.new: lest it entreat God and depart from you
does not have power to ascend

edits.old: given to the person as a cheerful spirit

problems.why: Grammatically awkward and unclear; 'given to the person cheerful' should be 'given to the person as cheerful' or 'given cheerful.' The Spirit was given to be cheerful.
problems.fix: given to the person to be cheerful
problems.ruling: τὸ δοθὲν...ἱλαρόν: Spirit given cheerful, not 'to the person cheerful.' Misreads grammar, misleads reader.

edits.new: given to the person to be cheerful

problems.why: Noun, adjective, and verb forms used for same concept; reader may miss connection

problems.quote: grief is more wicked than all the spirits and most terrible to the servants of God. Beyond all the spirits it destroys a person and rubs out the Holy Spirit, and yet it saves again
problems.fix: Explain paradox: grief over sin saves, grief from double-mindedness destroys

problems.quote: it destroys a person and rubs out the Holy Spirit, and yet it saves again.
problems.why: 'Rub out' is colloquial for 'kill'; applied to the Holy Spirit it is jarring and unclear.
Colloquial for 'kill'; applied to the Holy Spirit it should be 'extinguish' or 'quench'.

edits.old: grief is more wicked than all the spirits and most terrible to the servants of God. Beyond all the spirits it destroys a person and rubs out the Holy Spirit, and yet it saves again.
edits.new: grief is more wicked than all the spirits and most terrible to the servants of God. Beyond all the spirits it destroys a person and extinguishes the Holy Spirit, and yet it saves again.

edits.old: it destroys a person and rubs out the Holy Spirit, and yet it saves again.
edits.new: it destroys a person and extinguishes the Holy Spirit, and yet it saves again.

edits.old: how grief rubs out the Holy Spirit and yet saves again.
edits.new: how grief extinguishes the Holy Spirit and yet saves again.

edits.old: this grief enters into the person and grieves the Holy Spirit and rubs it out.
edits.new: this grief enters into the person and grieves the Holy Spirit and extinguishes it.

fixed: The glossary problem about double-mindedness is a style note, not a mistranslation; the English already uses the root consistently.
The paradox is present in the source (ἐκτρίβει...καὶ πάλιν σώζει) and is explained later in the passage; no edit needed.
Changed 'rub out' to 'extinguishes' in the first occurrence, as the colloquial sense is jarring for the Holy Spirit.
Changed 'rub out' to 'extinguishes' in the second occurrence.
Changed 'rubs out' to 'extinguishes' in the Shepherd's explanation.
Changed 'rubs it out' to 'extinguishes it' in the double-mindedness example.

notes.fix: Clarify: grief 'seems' to save by prompting repentance, but actually destroys by afflicting the Spirit.

last_rejected.why: Glossary does not contain ἱλαρότης, so no fixed term. However, checking if 'cheerfulness' matches sense: the glossary term ἱλαρότης is not listed, so free choice.
last_rejected.ruling: Glossary issue is non-substantive; 'cheerfulness' is a valid rendering of ἱλαρότητα.

last_rejected.why: 'Rubs out' suggests erasure by friction; ἐκτρίβει means 'wears out, destroys, crushes'—the Spirit is worn down/destroyed, not erased like pencil marks.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐκτρίβει literally means 'rubs out'; the metaphor is intentional and meaning is preserved.

last_rejected.why: 'Pagan friendships' could mean friendships with pagans, but ἐθνικαῖς here means 'worldly, Gentile-style'—friendships characterized by worldly/Gentile values, not necessarily with pagans.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐθνικαῖς means 'pagan/Gentile'; 'pagan friendships' is within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: and are corrupted and become barren
last_rejected.why: Missing 'destroyed' or 'ruined'—καταφθείρονται means 'destroyed/corrupted,' but the English 'corrupted' is present. Wait, let me re-read: 'are darkened by these activities and are corrupted and become barren'—this is present. No omission.
last_rejected.ruling: Reporter self-corrected: no omission exists; 'corrupted' renders καταφθείρονται.

last_rejected.quote: their mind is occupied with their own affairs
last_rejected.source_quote: ὁ νοῦς αὐτῶν περὶ τὴν πρᾶξιν αὐτῶν καταγίνεται
last_rejected.why: καταγίνεται means 'is brought down to, descends to, is fixed upon'—'occupied with' is too neutral; the Greek suggests degradation, being dragged down to.
last_rejected.fix: their mind is dragged down to their own affair
last_rejected.ruling: καταγίνεται means 'is occupied with'; 'occupied with' is within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: For every cheerful man does good things and thinks good things and despises grief
last_rejected.source_quote: πᾶς γὰρ ἱλαρὸς ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὰ ἐργάζεται καὶ ἀγαθὰ φρονεῖ καὶ καταφρονεῖ τῆς λύπης
last_rejected.why: 'Thinks good things' for φρονεῖ is weak—φρονεῖ means 'intends, purposes, has in mind,' not just 'thinks.'
last_rejected.ruling: φρονεῖ means 'thinks'; 'thinks good things' is within normal range.

last_rejected.why: 'Commits lawlessness' is literal but awkward; 'does lawlessness' or 'practices lawlessness' or 'acts lawlessly' would be more natural.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Commits lawlessness' is standard rendering of ἀνομίαν ἐργάζεται; mere style preference.

last_rejected.quote: For the intercession of a grieving man does not have power to ascend to the altar of God
last_rejected.source_quote: Πάντοτε γὰρ λυπηροῦ ἀνδρὸς ἡ ἔντευξις οὐκ ἔχει δύναμιν τοῦ ἀναβῆναι ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τοῦ θεοῦ
last_rejected.why: 'Does not have power to ascend' is awkward—'does not have the strength/power to ascend' or 'is not able to ascend.'
last_rejected.ruling: 'Does not have power to ascend' correctly renders οὐκ ἔχει δύναμιν; mere style preference.

last_rejected.source_quote: ἡ λύπη ἐγκάθηται εἰς τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ
last_rejected.why: 'Sits in' for ἐγκάθηται is weak—ἐγκάθηται means 'is enthroned in, is settled in, dwells in' with a sense of entrenched presence.
last_rejected.fix: grief is enthroned in his heart
last_rejected.ruling: ἐγκάθηται means 'sits in/dwells in'; 'sits in' is within normal range.

last_rejected.why: 'Pleasure' for ἡδονήν in this context of vinegar and wine mixing is odd—'taste' or 'flavor' or 'enjoyment' would be better; 'pleasure' suggests enjoyment rather than sensory quality.
last_rejected.ruling: ἡδονή means 'pleasure'; the analogy's point about lost enjoyment is preserved.

last_rejected.why: 'The same intercession' is unclear—'the same kind of intercession' or 'true intercession' or 'effective intercession' would clarify that grief ruins the quality of intercession.
last_rejected.ruling: τὴν αὐτὴν means 'the same'; 'the same intercession' is literal and adequate.

last_rejected.quote: and you will live to God
last_rejected.why: 'Live to God' is literal but unclear—'live for God' or 'live in God's sight' or 'have life with God.'
last_rejected.ruling: 'Live to God' is standard idiom for ζήσῃ τῷ θεῷ; meaning is clear.
